summary: Warren/Rappahannock lookout on Shenandoah NP's Hogback Mountain, built by CPS workers in 1942-43 and removed in 1962; the summit cabin was kept up to house comm gear, according to the WillhiteWeb page.

facts.design: lookout tower with a cabin on the summit, built by Civilian Public Service workers
facts.status_note: Lookout tower removed in 1962; the page says the old fire watchman's cabin was maintained to house electronic equipment for the Hogback communications towers (photos date from 1991-93, so current use is unverified)

access.note: Inside Shenandoah National Park; easily reached by Skyline Drive and the Appalachian Trail

notes_for_editor: Brief's record checks out: name, Warren / Rappahannock, coordinates and gone status match. The FFLA list has a second Hogback Mountain in Rockbridge County (37.90024, -79.48011), a different tower. The build and removal dates rest on one WillhiteWeb page; Wikipedia supports only location and access, not the tower history. WillhiteWeb gives the elevation as 3,474 feet; not stored since no fact key fits. The cabin photos on the page are dated 1991 to 1993, so the present-tense cabin description may be out of date. Do not confuse with the Warren County Fire Tower in North Carolina. The page writes only 'CPS'; 'Civilian Public Service' is the program's name and matches the page's description of CPS camps.
